tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Design of Peptides and Their Antibacterial Activity and Key Physicochemical Parameters
footnotes: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC, μM) was determined as the lowest concentration of a peptide that inhibited 95% of the bacterial growth. Data are representative of three independent experiments.

The geometric mean (GM) of the peptide MICs against bacteria and fungi was calculated. When no detectable antimicrobial activity was observed at 256 μM, a value of 512 μM was used to calculate the TI.

MHC is the minimum hemolytic concentration that caused 10% hemolysis of human erythrocytes. Data are representative of three independent experiments. When no detectable hemolytic activity was observed at 256 μM, a value of 512 μM was used to calculate the TI.
IC50 for GMC is the concentration of peptide corresponding to when the GMC growth was inhibited by 50%.
TI is the TI and calculated as MHC/GM. Larger values indicate greater cell selectivity.
Retention time (tR) on analytical reverse-phase (RP) HPLC.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: FIC of the Anoplin Analogues in Combination with Conventional Antibioticsa
footnotes: Fractional inhibitory concentration index (FIC) calculated using a checkerboard is defined according to the following equation: FIC = (MIC of peptide in combination)/(MIC of peptide alone) + (MIC of antibiotic in combination)/(MIC of antibiotic alone). FIC was interpreted as follows: FIC ≤0.5: synergy; 0.5 < FIC < 1: additive effect; 1.0 ≤ FIC < 4.0: indifference; and FIC ≥ 4: antagonism. We only selected the more active analogues along with antibiotics. “ND” means no detection.
